mainTopic: Kashering ovens, pots, knives and earthenware for פסח; cold versus hot absorption; and חמץ held as security for a loan
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא about an oven greased with אליה. Re-firing the oven makes it usable again, and this refutes רבא בר אהילאי. רבינא asks why רב then requires חמץ pots to be broken on פסח. רב אשי answers that the oven is metal and the pot is clay (חרס), or that the oven is heated from inside while the pot is heated from outside. The גמרא then gives practical rules for preparing utensils for פסח: knives and a wooden ladle are purged in boiling water in a כלי ראשון, because כבולעו כך פולטו. אמימר rules that glazed earthenware absorbs and can never be kashered for פסח, even though such vessels are permitted for יין נסך, because hot use absorbs far more than cold use. שמואל adds that vessels used only for cold חמץ are permitted, except containers of strong leaven: a בית שאור, a בית חרוסת, and the kneading bowls of מחוזא. A new משנה then teaches whether חמץ held as security for a loan is permitted after פסח. The גמרא starts to analyze it through the מחלוקת of אביי and רבא about when a creditor's collection takes effect, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A teaching about an oven greased with sheep-tail fat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that you may not grease an oven with אליה. If you did, bread baked in it is forbidden until the oven is fired up again.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not grease the inside of an oven with sheep-tail fat. If someone did grease it, all the bread baked in it is forbidden, until he fires up the oven again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as a source to test the view of רבא בר אהילאי. This step sets up the inference that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליה is meat fat, so bread baked in a greased oven picks up a meaty taste. Someone might then eat that bread with dairy, so the bread is forbidden. The key words are 'until he fires up the oven': they hint that a fresh firing burns off the fat and ends the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: fat tail of a sheep (meat fat)
that he heats or fires it up

steps.confusionAlert: The bread is not forbidden because it is literally meat. It is forbidden as a safeguard, so that people do not end up eating it with dairy (בשר בחלב).

phrases.english: One may not smear the oven with sheep-tail fat.
And if he did smear it,
all of the bread is forbidden,
phrases.notes: Because it might be eaten with dairy.

phrases.english: until he fires up the oven.
phrases.notes: Keep this phrase in mind; the next step builds on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין טָשִׁין אֶת הַתַּנּוּר בְּאַלְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A source brought in, continuing from the earlier part of the daf, to test the view of רבא בר אהילאי.
steps.raayaObject: Whether re-firing an oven removes the absorbed fat.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about greasing an oven with אליה.

steps.title: Inference: once the oven is fired, the bread is allowed
steps.stepSummary: From the word 'until', the גמרא reads the ברייתא to mean that after the oven is re-fired, bread baked in it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that once the oven was fired up, it is permitted after all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a precise inference from the ברייתא's wording. That inference becomes a challenge to רבא בר אהילאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר אהילאי held that bread from such an oven stays forbidden forever, even after firing. The ברייתא's 'until' shows the ban does end once the oven is fired. So his view clashes with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: this implies, from this we can infer

phrases.english: This implies that if the oven was fired up,
it is permitted in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא הוּסַּק הַתַּנּוּר מִיהָא שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא בר אהילאי's view that the bread is forbidden forever.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits the ban with 'until he fires it', so firing must remove the problem.

steps.title: רבא בר אהילאי is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a conclusive refutation of רבא בר אהילאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבא בר אהילאי. It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבא בר אהילאי's view cannot stand against the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תיובתא is said twice. The first time raises the refutation, and the second confirms it, meaning there is no answer. The הלכה is that re-firing an oven makes it usable again.
steps.whatToRemember: Firing up an oven again burns out the forbidden taste it absorbed, so the oven can be used again.
steps.confusionAlert: When תיובתא appears twice, it is not a repetition by mistake. The second one is the גמרא's final verdict that the refutation holds.

phrases.english: A refutation of Rava bar Ahilai,
it is indeed a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרָבָא בַּר אֲהִילַאי תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the challenge raised in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא בר אהילאי is rejected. Re-firing an oven makes it permitted.

steps.title: רבינא asks: then why must חמץ pots be broken?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי: if heating fixes an oven, why does רב rule that pots used for חמץ must be broken on פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Since רבא בר אהילאי was refuted, why did רב say that pots must be broken on פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא uses the conclusion we just reached to challenge a different ruling, the ruling of רב about pots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If heating burns out an absorbed taste, then a חמץ pot could also just be heated. Breaking it would then be unnecessary. So רב's harsh ruling seems to contradict what we just concluded.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּאִיתּוֹתַב רָבָא בַּר אֲהִילַאי,
phrases.english: Since Rava bar Ahilai was refuted,
why did Rav say:
'Pots on Passover must be broken'?
phrases.notes: Pots in which חמץ was cooked.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּאִיתּוֹתַב רָבָא בַּר אֲהִילַאי אַמַּאי קָאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 3 to challenge רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that חמץ pots must be broken.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If heating purges an oven, heating should purge a pot too, so there is no need to break it.

steps.title: First answer: a metal oven versus a clay pot
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the oven in the ברייתא is metal, while רב is talking about a clay pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, it is a metal oven. Here, it is a clay pot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי resolves the contradiction by showing that the two cases involve different materials.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Metal can be cleaned out by fire. חרס (earthenware) soaks taste deep inside, and fire never fully removes it. So the clay pot must be broken, while the metal oven is fixed by heating.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of כשרות: כלי חרס that absorbed a forbidden taste cannot be kashered.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There, it is a metal oven,
here, it is an earthenware pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם תַּנּוּר שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת הָכָא בִּקְדֵירָה שֶׁל חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oven and pot are the same, so heating should work for both.
steps.terutzMaskana: Metal is purged by fire, but clay is not.

steps.title: Second answer: heated from inside versus from outside
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, both are clay. The oven is heated from the inside, while the pot is heated from the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say that both are clay. This one is heated from the inside, and that one is heated from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to answer רבינא, without saying the oven is metal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oven has fire burning inside it, right where the absorbed taste is, so the taste burns out. A pot sits on the fire, so the heat comes from outside and does not purge the taste absorbed inside. The difference here is the direction of the heat, not the material.

keyTerms.meaning: or if you want, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
both this and that are of earthenware.
This one (the oven) is heated from the inside,
and that one (the pot) is heated from the outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא הָא וְהָא בְּשֶׁל חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 4, replacing the answer in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by how they are heated
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe all clay is the same and cannot be purged.
steps.terutzMaskana: Clay heated from the inside, where the taste is, does get purged.

steps.title: So heat the pot from the inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: then the owner should simply heat the pot from the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: so too, let him heat it from the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the second answer. If heating from the inside works, why not do that to the pot?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the direction of heat is all that matters, the pot could be saved by putting fire or coals inside it. That would make breaking it unnecessary again.

phrases.english: And if you say:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי לֶיעְבַּד לֵיהּ הַסָּקָה מִבִּפְנִים —
phrases.english: so too, let him heat it from the inside —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי לֶיעְבַּד לֵיהּ הַסָּקָה מִבִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a clay pot cannot be purged.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If heating from the inside works for the oven, it should work for the pot too.

steps.title: He will hold back for fear the pot cracks
steps.stepSummary: The owner cares about his pot and fears it will crack, so he will not heat it enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will spare it, because it might crack.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we cannot rely on the owner to heat the pot properly from the inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strong fire inside a pot might burst it, so the owner will go easy on the heat. Then the חמץ taste will not be fully burned out. That is why רב requires breaking the pot.

keyTerms.meaning: he cares about it, he spares it
that it will crack or burst

phrases.english: He spares it, because it might crack.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָיֵיס עֲלֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם דְּפָקְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A practical concern about human behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could simply heat the pot from the inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: He will not heat it fully, so we do not trust it.

steps.title: Practical rule for a clay baking griddle
steps.stepSummary: A בוכיא is heated from the outside, so it is forbidden. If it is filled with burning coals, it is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, this griddle is heated from the outside, and it is forbidden. But if he fills it with burning coals, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the inside/outside principle to a practical case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בוכיא is normally heated from outside, so firing it does not purge it. Filling it with burning coals heats it from the inside. Because this utensil is used to strong heat anyway, the owner is not afraid to fire it fully, and that works.
steps.whatToRemember: Clay absorbs taste. Heating from the outside does not purge it. Strong heating from the inside, such as filling it with coals, works when there is no fear of cracking.

phrases.english: Therefore, this griddle
is heated from the outside, and it is forbidden,
but if he fills it with burning coals,
it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ הַאי בּוּכְיָא הֶסֵּיקוֹ מִבַּחוּץ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from steps 6 to 8 to a practical case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A clay utensil heated from outside cannot be purged. Filling it with coals heats it from inside, and that does purge it.

steps.title: רבינא asks how to prepare knives for פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי how knives are made ready for use on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: These knives, how do we prepare them for פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רבינא asks a practical question about how to make knives fit for פסח use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knives are used all year with hot חמץ food, so they may have absorbed חמץ taste. A knife is also tricky because it has a metal blade and usually a wooden handle. That is why it needs its own discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: how do we do / how do we deal with

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
these knives, on Passover,
how do we treat them?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי סַכִּינֵי בְּפִסְחָא הֵיכִי עָבְדִינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from heating ovens and pots (Steps 5-9) to a new utensil: knives.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The procedure for making knives fit for פסח use.

steps.title: רב אשי says he makes new knives
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that for himself, he has new knives made.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For me, we make new ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a personal answer. He simply uses brand-new knives for פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New knives have never touched חמץ, so the problem goes away completely. However, this answer avoids the real question of how to fix an old knife. That opening is what רבינא pushes on next.

phrases.english: He said to him: For me,
we make new ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידִי חַדְתָּא קָא עָבְדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question in a personal way.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אשי uses new knives for פסח.

steps.title: רבינא objects: what about someone who cannot afford new knives
steps.stepSummary: רבינא points out that not everyone can buy new knives, so what should they do?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That works for you, Master, since you are able to. But what about someone who is not able?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי's answer. It only helps wealthy people, and he wants a solution for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is practical, not a contradiction from a source. Buying new knives is not a general halachic method. רבינא needs a way to make an existing knife usable.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is fine for Master,
who is able to,
but one who is not able, what?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח מָר דְּאֶפְשָׁר לֵיהּ, דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר לֵיהּ מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 11 as too limited.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's answer of using new knives.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A solution that only works for people who can afford new knives does not answer the general question.

steps.title: רב אשי explains he meant making knives like new
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי clarifies that he meant making old knives "like new." Cover the handles in mud, heat the blades in fire, then put the handles in boiling water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I meant "like new." Their handles go in mud, their metal goes in fire, and then I put their handles in boiling water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that he was really describing a method for old knives. The method is a detailed cleaning process that makes them as good as new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mud protects the wooden handle while the metal blade is heated in fire (ליבון). The handle cannot go into fire, so it is then purged separately in boiling water (הגעלה). Each part gets the treatment it can handle.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי did not change his answer. He is explaining that "new" really meant "like new," which is a method anyone can use.

phrases.english: He said to him: I,
meant "like new":
their handles in mud,
and their metal in fire,
and then I put their handles into boiling water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא, כְּעֵין חַדְתָּא קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's objection by reinterpreting "new" as "like new."
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי seemed to mean literally buying new knives.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant a procedure that makes old knives like new: ליבון for the blade and boiling water for the handle.

steps.title: The הלכה: boiling water in a first vessel suffices for blade and handle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that both blade and handle only need boiling water in a כלי ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: both this and that, in boiling water and in a first vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling. Both the blade and the handle are fixed with boiling water, as long as it is in a כלי ראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's fire treatment for the blade was more than necessary. The הלכה is more lenient: the blade does not need fire. The water must still be in the pot it was boiled in (כלי ראשון), not poured into another vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: first vessel: the pot heated directly on the fire

steps.whatToRemember: Knives for פסח: both blade and handle can be purged with boiling water in a כלי ראשון. Fire is not required for the blade.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: both this and that
in boiling water and in a first vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּרוֹתְחִין וּבִכְלִי רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the practical halacha, which is more lenient than רב אשי's own practice for the blade.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both blade and handle of a knife are made fit for פסח with boiling water in a כלי ראשון.

steps.title: A wooden ladle is purged in boiling water in a first vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rules that a wooden ladle is purged in boiling water in a כלי ראשון. The reason is כבולעו כך פולטו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: A wooden ladle is purged in boiling water in a first vessel. He holds: as it absorbs, so it releases.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement about another utensil, a wooden ladle. The גמרא also explains the reasoning behind the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ladle absorbed חמץ taste by being stirred in a pot boiling on the fire, which is a כלי ראשון. By the rule כבולעו כך פולטו, the same level of heat will draw the taste back out. So boiling water in a כלי ראשון is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: as it absorbs, so it releases

steps.whyThisMatters: כבולעו כך פולטו is a foundational rule of הכשר כלים. The method used to purge a utensil matches the way it absorbed the forbidden taste.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
a wooden ladle, one purges it
in boiling water and in a first vessel.
He holds: as it absorbs, so it releases.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עֵץ פָּרוּר מַגְעִילוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling for another utensil, using the same כלי ראשון method as Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wooden ladle is kashered for פסח with boiling water in a כלי ראשון, because כבולעו כך פולטו.

steps.title: אמימר is asked about glazed earthenware vessels
steps.stepSummary: אמימר is asked whether glazed earthenware vessels (מאני דקוניא) may be used on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked אמימר: These glazed vessels, may one use them on פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is raised before אמימר about glazed clay vessels. The question is whether their glaze lets them be used on פסח after being used with חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain כלי חרס absorbs and cannot be kashered. The question is whether a glaze coating seals the clay so it does not absorb.

phrases.english: They asked Ameimar:
these glazed vessels,
what is the law about using them on Passover?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵאַמֵּימָר הָנֵי מָאנֵי דְקוּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wood and metal utensils to glazed earthenware.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether glazed earthenware used with חמץ may be used on פסח.

steps.title: Narrowing the question to smooth black and white glazed vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the question. Green glaze and cracked vessels are certainly forbidden. The doubt is only about smooth black or white glazed vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Green ones, don't ask, since they are certainly forbidden. Ask about black and white ones: what? And where they have cracks, don't ask, since they are certainly forbidden. Ask about smooth ones: what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the question by removing the obvious cases. This sets up exactly what אמימר must answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Green glaze clearly does not stop absorption, and cracks trap חמץ, so those cases are obviously forbidden. That leaves one real doubt: black or white glaze on a smooth vessel with no cracks.

phrases.english: green ones, you need not ask —
for they are certainly forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אוּכָּמֵי וְחִיוָּרֵי, מַאי?
phrases.english: Where you should ask is black and white ones: what?
And where they have cracks,
you need not ask, for they are certainly forbidden.
Where you should ask is smooth ones: what?

steps.triggerLanguage: יְרוּקָּא לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ דְּוַדַּאי אֲסִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question of Step 16 to its true point of doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The status of smooth, black or white glazed earthenware without cracks.

steps.title: אמימר rules glazed earthenware is forbidden because it absorbs
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says he sees liquid seep through these vessels, so they absorb and are forbidden. The Torah testified that a כלי חרס never leaves its flawed state.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I see that they sweat. So they absorb and are forbidden. And the Torah testified about an earthenware vessel that it never leaves its flaw.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives his ruling: even smooth black or white glazed vessels are forbidden on פסח. He backs this with what he observed and with a Torah principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquid seeping to the outside proves that the glaze does not seal the clay, so it absorbs חמץ. Once it absorbs, it is treated like any כלי חרס. The Torah requires a כלי חרס to be broken rather than purged, so it can never be kashered.

keyTerms.meaning: that they sweat / let liquid seep out

steps.whatToRemember: Glazed earthenware used with חמץ is forbidden on פסח, even smooth black or white ones. It absorbs, and a כלי חרס can never be kashered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that glazing does not save a כלי חרס. Earthenware is treated as permanently unable to release what it absorbed.

phrases.english: He said to him: I see that they sweat,
so evidently they absorb, and they are forbidden.
And the Torah testified about an earthenware vessel
that it never leaves its flawed state.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ דְּמִידַיְּיתֵי אַלְמָא בָּלְעִי וַאֲסִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the narrowed question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even smooth black or white glazed earthenware absorbs, so it is forbidden on פסח and cannot be kashered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Glazed כלי חרס is forbidden on פסח because it absorbs, and a כלי חרס never leaves its flawed state.

steps.title: Why are glazed vessels permitted for libation wine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אמימר using מרימר's ruling that glazed vessels of every color are permitted for יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about libation wine? מרימר taught that glazed vessels are permitted whether they are black, white, or green.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אמימר's strict ruling. For יין נסך, glazed vessels are permitted, so why are they forbidden for חמץ?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר just said glazed vessels absorb, so they cannot be used on פסח. Yet מרימר permits the very same vessels after they held gentile wine, even green-glazed ones. If they absorb, they should be forbidden there too.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured for idol worship; any wine touched by a gentile is suspected of this
What is different? (a challenge pointing out a contradiction)

phrases.english: And what is different regarding libation wine,
as Mareimar expounded:
Glazed vessels,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין אוּכָּמֵא בֵּין חִיוָּרֵי וּבֵין יְרוּקֵּי
phrases.english: whether black, whether white, or whether green
are permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא לְעִנְיַן יֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling in step 18 using a contradictory ruling about יין נסך
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that glazed vessels absorb and are forbidden on פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same vessels are treated as non-absorbing for יין נסך, even green ones, so they should not be treated as absorbing for חמץ.

steps.title: Rabbinic laws follow the Torah's pattern
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer: one cannot say יין נסך is lenient just because it is rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that יין נסך is rabbinic while חמץ is from the Torah, that does not work. Whatever the Rabbis enacted, they enacted in the pattern of Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down an easy answer before anyone can use it. That keeps the challenge alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the Rabbis were lenient with יין נסך because it is only their own law. The גמרא rejects this. When the Rabbis make a rule, they model it on Torah law, so the same rules of absorption should apply.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer, often to reject it)

keyTerms.term: כׇּל דְּתַקּוּן רַבָּנַן כְּעֵין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא תַּקּוּן
keyTerms.meaning: Whatever the Rabbis enacted, they enacted like Torah law

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule used throughout ש"ס: rabbinic laws are usually built to mirror the structure of Torah laws.

phrases.english: And if you say:
libation wine is rabbinic,
while chametz is from the Torah,
whatever the Rabbis instituted,
they instituted similar to Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 19 by rejecting a possible answer in advance
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed answer that rabbinic יין נסך can be more lenient than Torah-level חמץ
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Rabbinic enactments follow the pattern of Torah law, so they cannot be dismissed as automatically lenient.

steps.title: Hot use versus cold use
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that the two cases differ: cooking vessels are used with hot food, while wine vessels hold cold liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This vessel is used with hot food, and that vessel is used with cold liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר resolves the contradiction. The difference is not about how serious the prohibition is. It is about how the vessel is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessels in question for פסח were used all year for cooking hot חמץ, and heat makes the walls absorb a lot of taste. Wine vessels only store cold wine, which absorbs far less. So glazed vessels are permitted after holding gentile wine but forbidden after holding חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Its use (how the vessel is normally used)

steps.whatToRemember: How much a vessel absorbs depends on its normal use. Hot use absorbs much more than cold use.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This one is used with hot substances,
and that one is used with cold substances.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זֶה תַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ עַל יְדֵי חַמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 19–20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the vessel's manner of use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The glazed vessels should be treated the same for יין נסך and חמץ
steps.terutzMaskana: Hot use causes absorption and cold use does not, so the rulings differ

steps.title: Vessels used cold for חמץ may be used for מצה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that vessels used for חמץ only while cold may be used for מצה, except a בית שאור, whose leavening is strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר אבא said in the name of רב חייא בר אשי, who said in the name of שמואל: Any vessel used for cold חמץ may be used for מצה, except the sourdough container, because its leavening is strong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling that continues the hot-versus-cold theme. It gives a general rule and one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cold חמץ does not soak into a vessel's walls, so the vessel needs no הכשרה. The בית שאור stored strong leaven for a long time. That makes it absorb even without heat, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A container for storing sourdough starter (leaven)
Its leavening is strong or potent

phrases.english: Rava bar Abba said
that Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said
that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמְּשׁוּ בָּהֶן חָמֵץ בְּצוֹנֵן
phrases.english: All vessels in which chametz was used cold
one may use them for matzah,
except for the sourdough container,
since its leavening is strong.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the hot/cold distinction from step 21 with a new ruling about cold use
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels used for cold חמץ are permitted for מצה, except a בית שאור, because strong leaven is absorbed even cold.

steps.title: The spice container is like the sourdough container
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds that a container for חרוסת is like a בית שאור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The container for חרוסת is like the sourdough container, whose leavening is strong.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds one more item to שמואל's exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חרוסת here is a sharp mixture that contained flour, so it was strongly fermented. Like sourdough, it soaks into the vessel even without heat.

keyTerms.meaning: A container for a sharp, fermented spice mixture containing flour
Is similar to, has the same status

steps.confusionAlert: This חרוסת is not the sweet dip used at the סדר. It is a sharp spice mixture that contained flour.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And the spice-mixture container
is like the sourdough container whose leavening is strong.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וּבֵית חֲרוֹסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the exception in שמואל's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית חרוסת has the same status as a בית שאור.

steps.title: The kneading bowls of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the bowls of מחוזא are like a בית שאור, because dough is regularly kneaded and left to stand in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The bowls of מחוזא are regularly used for kneading חמץ dough, and the dough is left to rise in them. So they are like the sourdough container, whose leavening is strong.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another case to the same exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These bowls were not only used briefly. Leavened dough was kneaded in them often and left there to rise. That repeated, lasting contact makes them absorb like a בית שאור.

keyTerms.meaning: They leave it standing (for a long time)

phrases.english: Rava said:
These bowls of Mechoza,
since they are regularly used to knead leavened dough in them,
and they leave the leavened dough standing in them,
they are like the sourdough container whose leavening is strong.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי אַגָּנֵי דְמָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case to the בית שאור exception
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bowls of מחוזא used regularly for kneading and storing dough are like a בית שאור.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רבא's ruling teaches anything new. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If dough is often kneaded and left in these bowls, they plainly seem like a בית שאור. So why did רבא need to state it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (a challenge that a statement adds nothing new)

phrases.english: Isn't it obvious?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא's statement in step 24 is needed
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling about the bowls of מחוזא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bowls clearly match the reasoning of בית שאור, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Wide bowls might seem not to absorb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one might have thought the wide bowls are aired out and do not absorb, so רבא teaches that they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that since the bowls are wide, the air reaches them and they do not absorb. So he teaches us that they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point of רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית שאור is a closed container. These bowls are open and wide, so one could think air weakens the leaven and stops absorption. רבא teaches that frequent use still makes them absorb.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

phrases.english: You might have said:
since they are wide,
the air dominates them
and they do not absorb,
he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: identifies a plausible mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wide, open bowls are aired out and do not absorb
steps.terutzMaskana: Even wide bowls absorb when they are used often for leavened dough
steps.whatToRemember: Cold חמץ usually does not require הכשרה of a vessel. Containers with strong or long-standing leaven are the exception: a בית שאור, a בית חרוסת, and the bowls of מחוזא.

steps.title: משנה: חמץ held as security for a loan
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that חמץ securing a gentile's loan to a Jew is permitted after פסח, but חמץ securing a Jew's loan to a gentile is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a gentile lent money to a Jew, with the Jew's חמץ as security, it is permitted to benefit from it after פסח. If a Jew lent money to a gentile, with the gentile's חמץ as security, it is forbidden to benefit from it after פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It shifts from vessels to the question of who owned חמץ over פסח when it was security for a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is who counts as the owner of the חמץ during פסח. When the gentile holds it as security, it is treated as his, so it is permitted afterward. When the Jew holds the gentile's חמץ as security, it is treated as the Jew's, so it falls under the ban on חמץ owned by a Jew over פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Against his חמץ (with it as security)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that חמץ which a Jew owned during פסח is forbidden even after פסח. Ownership through a loan and its security decides the outcome.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל חֲמֵצוֹ,
phrases.english: A gentile who lent money to a Jew against his chametz,
after Passover, it is permitted to derive benefit from it.

phrases.aramaic: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת גּוֹי עַל חֲמֵצוֹ,
phrases.english: And a Jew who lent money to a gentile against his chametz,
after Passover, it is forbidden to derive benefit from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ גּוֹי שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל חֲמֵצוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ securing a gentile's loan to a Jew is permitted after פסח. חמץ securing a Jew's loan to a gentile is forbidden after פסח.

steps.title: When does the creditor's ownership begin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת. אביי says a בעל חוב collects the collateral retroactively, and רבא says he collects it only from now on.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was stated about a creditor: אביי said he collects retroactively. רבא said he collects from now on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה by quoting a disagreement between אביי and רבא about when a creditor's ownership of collateral begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that once the creditor collects, we look at the property as if it was his from the time of the loan (למפרע). רבא holds that it becomes his only from the time of collection (מכאן ולהבא). This matters for our משנה because the question is whose חמץ it was during פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was stated." This introduces a disagreement between אמוראים.
A creditor, the one who lent money.
Retroactively, looking back to an earlier time.
From now on, only going forward.
Collects payment of a debt, here by taking the collateral.

steps.confusionAlert: Both אביי and רבא agree that the creditor collects in the end. They argue only about when the property counts as his: from the time of the loan, or from the time of collection.
steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת is the key to the משנה. If the creditor's ownership goes back in time, then חמץ held as collateral may count as the creditor's during פסח.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated: a creditor,
phrases.notes: איתמר signals a disagreement between אמוראים.

phrases.english: Abaye said: he collects retroactively.
phrases.notes: The property counts as his from the time of the loan.

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא אָמַר: מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא גּוֹבֶה.
phrases.english: And Rava said: he collects from here and onward.
phrases.notes: The property becomes his only from the time of collection.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: בַּעַל חוֹב, אַבָּיֵי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה about חמץ held as security for a loan, by bringing a basic rule of loan law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: a creditor's collection takes effect retroactively from the time of the loan. רבא: it takes effect only from the time of collection.

steps.title: Sale or consecration: everyone agrees the creditor seizes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the מחלוקת. If the borrower consecrated or sold the field, all agree that the lender can come and take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anywhere that the borrower consecrated the field or the borrower sold it, everyone agrees that the lender comes and seizes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to limit the argument between אביי and רבא by naming a case where they both agree. The sentence is not finished yet, so this is setting up the next move: where they actually disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower sold the field or gave it to הקדש after taking the loan, the lender can still take it from the buyer or from הקדש. This is because the lender's claim on the field (the lien) came before the sale. So even רבא agrees here, and the מחלוקת must be about some other kind of case.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated, meaning he gave the field to הקדש.
Seizes, meaning he takes the property from the person who now holds it.
"Everyone does not disagree," meaning all opinions agree.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude from this case that רבא agrees with אביי. The creditor here wins because his lien came before the sale, not because collection works retroactively. The real disagreement is still to come.

phrases.english: Anywhere that the borrower consecrated
phrases.notes: He gave the mortgaged field to הקדש.

phrases.english: or the borrower sold it —
phrases.notes: He sold the mortgaged field to someone else.

phrases.english: everyone agrees
that the lender comes and seizes it,
phrases.notes: The lender's claim on the field came before the sale, so it wins. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּאַקְדֵּישׁ לֹוֶה וְזַבֵּין לֹוֶה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the מחלוקת from Step 28 by naming a case where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the borrower sold or consecrated the mortgaged field, all agree that the lender may seize it, because his lien came before the sale.
